Definition: to spread out (i.e. deploy in hostile array); by analogy, to strip (i.e. unclothe, plunder, flay, etc.)
BiblicalUsage: Pashat means to spread out, to strip off, to raid and plunder. Jonathan strips himself of his robe and gives it to David in 1 Samuel 18:4, and Saul strips off his clothes and prophesies in 1 Samuel 19:24. The Philistines strip Saul in 1 Chronicles 10:8 when they find him slain on Mount Gilboa, and David raids the Geshurites and the Amalekites in 1 Samuel 27:8.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the stripping in these verses tells the story of two kings: Jonathan strips himself to honour David, Saul is stripped by his enemies, and the robe that is given freely is worth more than the armour that is taken. I hold that the robe given freely honours the giver, and the armour taken by force only proves the taker.
